title: Expired Delegation Authority on Capital Expenditure Approval
scenario_text:
During the Q1 SOX walkthrough for the capital expenditure cycle at Ironforge Manufacturing's Cleveland plant, you pull the following evidence for a $1.2M CNC machine purchase (PO 4500089234):

**SAP S/4HANA — Transaction ME23N (PO Display), PO 4500089234**
Vendor: Haas Automation (VM-00412) | Material: CNC-5AX-UMC1600 | Net value: $1,187,400
Created by: T.NGUYEN | Created: 2026-01-28
Release strategy: 2-step | Release 1: M.KOWALSKI (2026-01-29) | Release 2: D.PATEL (2026-01-30)
Release indicator: Fully released

**SharePoint — /internal-audit/workpapers/delegation-matrix-2025.xlsx**
Row 47: D.PATEL | Delegated authority from: R.VASQUEZ (VP Operations) | Authority: Approve CapEx up to $1.5M | Effective: 2025-10-01 | Expiry: 2026-01-15 | Status: Not renewed
[Version history shows this file was last updated by HR on 2026-01-20 to reflect Patel's delegation expiry]

**Microsoft Teams — #capex-approvals (2026-01-14, 3:47 PM)**
@R.Vasquez: Heads up team — I'm extending Deepak's delegation through end of Q1. Will send the updated form to GRC tomorrow.
@D.Patel: 👍
[No further messages in thread. No updated delegation form found in MasterControl or SharePoint.]

**SAP — SU53 Authorization Check (pulled during audit)**
User D.PATEL | Auth object: M_EINK_FRG | Release group: 02 | Release code: VP | Status: Active
[SAP role was never deactivated — technical access persists regardless of delegation matrix]

**MasterControl — Document search for 'Delegation of Authority'**
DOC-2025-DA-091: Delegation form for D.PATEL | Effective 2025-10-01 | Expiry 2026-01-15 | Signed by R.VASQUEZ
No subsequent delegation document found. Last DOA policy revision (POL-FIN-003 Rev 7) states: 'Delegations must be documented in MasterControl with wet or electronic signature. Verbal or informal extensions are not valid for SOX-controlled processes.'

**Outlook — Email from D.Patel to Internal Audit (2026-02-10, during fieldwork)**
Subject: RE: CapEx walkthrough — PO 4500089234
'Hi Franklin — Raj told me the delegation was being extended. I saw his Teams message and assumed it was handled. The PO was urgent because the machine lead time is 14 weeks and we'd miss the Q2 production ramp if we waited.'
question: Based on COSO framework and Ironforge's documented controls, how should this finding be classified for the SOX audit?

contributor.name: Franklin Owens
contributor.title: Internal Audit Manager
contributor.domain_expertise: SOX compliance, control testing, approval authority verification, delegation matrix enforcement

choices: Control deficiency — the delegation expired and the approval lacked valid documented authority, but compensating controls (SAP release strategy, amount within threshold) reduce severity below significant deficiency
Not a deficiency — R.Vasquez clearly communicated intent to extend the delegation in Teams, and the approval was within the originally authorized dollar threshold

Significant deficiency — the control owner's delegation was expired and no valid extension existed in the system of record; the SAP technical access remaining active represents an IT general control gap that compounds the issue
Material weakness — management override of the delegation control represents a pervasive breakdown requiring disclosure to the audit committee
